ns2:section.sectionText: Prerequisite for Spring 2018: Math 461 or Math 463. This special section of Math 476 is restricted to mathematics majors. The syllabus will not reflect the new SOA exam Investments & Financial Markets that is offered starting July 2018. In this course, we discuss the theoretical foundation for financial models and their applications to insurance and other financial risks. We define and consider the basic properties of financial derivatives widely used in today's markets, such as forward contracts and call and put options. We also discuss more complicated option strategies such as spreads, collars, butterfly spreads, and iron condors. We study financial, commodity, and interest rate forward contracts and futures as well as interest rate swaps. A central problem for all these derivatives is the pricing of the derivatives. For this purpose, we discuss the binomial option pricing model that illustrates certain basic principles. We also mention the famous Black-Scholes formula for option pricing that played a role in making option markets more understandable and hence contributed to their enormous growth from the 1970s onwards. If time allows, a few further pricing and risk management topics will be considered.
